The 8 games (currently being added to the sellable catalog by a separate parallel task, so their `lib/games.ts` entries may or may not exist yet depending on timing — check first; if an entry already exists, just add the art slug key and files; if it doesn't exist yet, wait/retry by checking again, since another task is actively adding these entries concurrently — do NOT create your own competing `lib/games.ts` entries for these games, only add art file paths and the `GAME_ART_SLUG` poster/hero keys once the base entry exists):

1. ARK: Survival Ascended
2. Soulmask
3. Don't Starve Together
4. Vintage Story
5. Necesse
6. Team Fortress 2
7. DayZ
8. Left 4 Dead 2

Check `public/games/art/` for the existing naming convention: `{slug}_hero.jpg` (1200-wide landscape), `{slug}_poster.jpg` (300x450 portrait), `{slug}_logo.png` (transparent logo, 640x360 canvas). Check `lib/games.ts` for each game's exact `GAME_ART_SLUG` key/slug string once its entry exists.

For each game, source REAL official promotional art from Steam's public CDN (the same legitimate approach used for the previous 5 games and for every existing game on the site) — e.g. `https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/{appid}/library_hero.jpg`, `library_600x900_2x.jpg` (or `_2x` variants), `logo.png`, or `shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/...` for the same asset types. Find each game's correct Steam App ID via WebSearch/SteamDB if not already known (ARK: Survival Ascended, Soulmask, Don't Starve Together, Necesse, TF2, DayZ, and Left 4 Dead 2 are all Steam-distributed; Vintage Story is NOT Steam-distributed — it's sold directly from vintagestory.at, so for Vintage Story specifically, source official art from its own website/press-kit instead, being careful to only use clearly official promotional/press assets, not a random fan screenshot).

Download, verify (visually confirm via the Read tool that each image actually shows the correct game before considering it done — do not save a broken/wrong image), resize/recompress with ImageMagick if needed to match the site's existing dimension/file-size conventions (check a couple of existing files as your target), and save into `public/games/art/` with the exact correct slug naming. Update `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG` entries to add the `poster` (and `logo` where available) keys for each game once its base entry exists (mirroring exactly what was done for the previous 5 games' art-slug wiring).

If a game's `lib/games.ts` entry doesn't exist yet when you check, you can still proceed to source and save the art files under the correct slug name (reasonably inferred from the game's obvious slug convention, e.g. `ark-asa` is already used for the existing ARK, so Survival Ascended likely needs a distinct slug like `ark-survival-ascended` or similar — check for hints/conventions, or just pick a sensible kebab-case slug and clearly report what you chose so it can be matched up) — just don't create or edit the `lib/games.ts` entry itself if it doesn't exist, to avoid conflicting with the other task's edits. Report the exact slug you used for each game so it can be wired up correctly afterward if the entry didn't exist yet.

Report back per-game (table, under 400 words): art sourced (hero/poster/logo yes/no), source, final dimensions/file size, slug used, and any gaps (e.g. if a game genuinely has no clean vertical capsule, same as the Dragonwilds case from earlier today — use the same workaround of cropping an official screenshot, and say so).
